written.text: Write a precis of the following passage, giving it a suitable title:(14) Communication is an essential requirement for all human performance and interaction. It welds individuals into groups by developing common interests, by crystallising common concepts, by establishing relationships, by extending cooperation, by sharing experience and by establishing a common heritage. The underlying principle of each of these acts is that we use language as a means of communication. In a much broader sense, language is a tool of communication, but aside from language, there is also another important, but often overlooked means of communication. When we talk about language as a means of communication, we mean the usage of language and words– how they sound, how they are formed, their meaning, and their structure. However, we do not use just words or language to communicate. Non-verbal communication– our body movements, our expressions and our gestures - convey so much more than we are aware of. In fact, it is often said that a person may lie with their words, but their bodies reveal the truth. When someone’s body language is inconsistent with their words, we tend to believe the body language rather than the words. Thus, both these means of communication– verbal and non-verbal, are both essential in effective communication. For example, a person may say that they are interested in what we are talking about, but if they fidget constantly, or their eyes keep darting away, or their legs are angled away from us, their body movements convey that they are either distracted, or they are not interested in what we have to say. This is why, to excel in communication, it is important to focus on both what we are saying, but on what our bodies are conveying. A pleasant facial expression, open gestures, and correct posture suggests that you are confident, honest and invested in what you are trying to express. No matter the content of the speech, if the speaker just drones on without making eye contact with the audience, or he crosses his arms, the audience will find it hard to fully connect with him or what he is saying. The most effective communication, therefore, incorporates the skillful usage of both verbal and non-verbal means of communication.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:- From the wealth of science we have selected certain parts. And our choice has in no way been influenced by a consideration of the higher interest of humanity. It has simply followed the path of our natural tendencies. The principles of the greatest convenience and of the least effort, the pleasure to be had from speed, change, and comfort, and also the burning need of escaping from ourselves, are the driving force in the success of new inventions. But no one has ever stopped to ask how we would cope with the enormous acceleration of the pace of life resulting from rapid transportation, telegraph, telephone, modern business methods, machines that write and calculate, and those that do all the housekeeping drudgery of former times. Steam-heated houses, electric lighting, elevators, and the chemical doctoring and adulteration of foodstuffs have been accepted lock, stock, and barrel, their comprehensive adoption being solely precipitated by the hedonic and facilitative advantages they confer. Nevertheless, no account whatsoever has been taken of their probable effect on human beings. In the organization of industrial life, the influence of the factory upon the physiological and mental state of the workers has been left by the wayside. Modern industry is based on the conception of the maximum production at lowest cost so that an individual or a group of individuals may rake in as much money as possible. It has expanded without any idea of the true nature of the human beings who run the machines, and without giving a second thought to the effect produced on the individuals and on their descendants by the artificial mode of existence imposed by the factory. The great cities have been built with no regard for us. The shape and dimensions of the skyscrapers hinge entirely on the necessity of obtaining the maximum income per square foot of ground, and of offering to the tenants’ offices and apartments that please them. This caused the construction of gigantic buildings where far too many human beings are crammed together. Civilized men have a taste for such a way of living. While they soak up the comfort and banal luxury of their dwelling, they do not realise that they are missing out on the necessities of life. A modern city consists of monstrous edifices and of dark, narrow streets chock-full of gasoline fumes, coal dust and toxic gases, shattered by the noise of the taxi cabs, trucks, and trolleys, and swarming ceaselessly with great crowds. Obviously, it has not been planned for the good of its inhabitants. Our life is influenced to a great extent by commercial advertising. Such publicity is undertaken purely and simply in the interest of the advertisers and not of the consumers. For example, the public has been hoodwinked into believing that white bread is better than brown. Consequently, flour has been treated more and more thoroughly and thus stripped of its most useful components. Such treatment allows for its preservation for longer periods and facilitates the making of bread. The millers and the bakers line their pockets. The consumers eat an inferior product, under the impression that it is a superior one. And in the countries where bread is the principal food, the population goes downhill. Enormous amounts of money are poured into publicity. As a result, large quantities of pharmaceutical products that are at the least useless, and often harmful, have become the norm for civilized men. In this manner, the raw greed of individuals sufficiently shrewd to whip up a popular demand for the goods that they have for sale calls the shots in the modern world. (i)According to the passage, why have modern inventions and industrial developments been widely adopted without considering their effects on human beings?(2) (ii)Why does the author criticize modern industry’s approach to production?(2) (iii)According to the passage, what role does greed play in the modern world?(2) (iv)What is the meaning of the phrase ‘accepted lock, stock, and barrel’ used in the passage?
